result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks and signals, but is dominated by a wide, multi-lane roadway and commercial land uses with frequent driveway curb cuts. The lack of physical buffers and long crossing distances create a car-centric environment that prioritizes vehicle throughput over pedestrian comfort.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main intersection

hazards.name: Frequent driveway curb cuts
hazards.description: Multiple vehicle access points for the gas station and fast food restaurant create numerous conflict points across the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left sides of the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk is immediately adjacent to travel lanes with no physical separation or planting strip.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the edges of the roadway

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation
interventions.description: Reduce the number of curb cuts for adjacent commercial properties to minimize vehicle-pedestrian conflict points.

result.summary: The environment is highly car-oriented, characterized by a wide multi-lane roadway and a complete lack of pedestrian infrastructure on the near side. The far side features a large, open asphalt parking lot for a commercial business, creating a massive undefined conflict zone between vehicles and any potential pedestrians.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no paved walkway for pedestrians on the near side of the street, forcing them into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and left side of the image

hazards.name: Excessive Curb Cut Width
hazards.description: The commercial property has a wide, undefined asphalt entrance that creates a large conflict zone where vehicles can cross the pedestrian path at any point.
hazards.location_in_image: Center right, in front of the AutoZone building

hazards.name: Wide Unprotected Crossing
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway lacks any marked crossings or pedestrian refuge islands, making it dangerous to traverse.
hazards.location_in_image: Spanning the entire width of the road in the center

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on both sides of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Curbing
interventions.description: Install curbs and define specific, narrow driveway entrances to the commercial lot to reduce the area of conflict between cars and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a median refuge island to break up the long crossing distance and allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane arterial road with commercial and mixed-use buildings. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the environment is dominated by vehicle traffic with no visible pedestrian crossings or safety buffers in the immediate vicinity.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a significant distance without any refuge islands.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes encourage higher vehicle speeds, increasing the risk and severity of potential collisions.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffers
hazards.description: Sidewalks are directly adjacent to the roadway or parking lane with no physical buffer like trees or bollards.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk edges

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at intersections or mid-block to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes or lane widths to slow traffic and repurpose space for bike lanes or wider buffers.

result.summary: The image shows a typical urban mixed-use street with continuous sidewalks and active ground-floor commercial frontages. While the sidewalk is present and in good condition, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian safety features like marked crossings or traffic calming measures, and parked cars create visual obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked cars blocks the sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line on the left side of the street.

hazards.name: Lack of Mid-block Crossing
hazards.description: In a commercial area with high potential for pedestrian activity, there are no marked crossings visible, which may encourage unsafe mid-block crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire visible roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk to provide a designated and safer place for pedestrians to cross the street.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve sightlines.
